Added your suggestion.
If it's re-requesting FIRST_PART, then transfer_handle can be 0, right?

My understanding is that for the first part it will always be FIRST_PART, even the first part is being re-requested immediately. PLDM_XFER_CURRENT_PART will be used to re-request any middle or last segment.

> XFER_CURRENT_PART: The requester is asking for the part just sent to be retransmitted, such as if the
checksum of data cumulatively received did not match the DataIntegrityChecksum in the current part.

> To request retransmission of the current part of data (such as upon detection of a checksum error), the requester shall set TransferOperation to XFER_CURRENT_PART in the request message and shall set DataTransferHandle to the handle that was previously used with this part.

Those are all statements about XFER_CURRENT_PART in DSP0240_1.2.0. From those points, if CRC for first part mis-matches, we can totally re-request first part by using XFER_CURRENT_PART and setting DataTransferHandle to the previous handle (which is 0 for first part).
